title.narrative: Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises Development Program (Subprogram 1)

description.narrative:
The proposed Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises Development Program aims to support the Government of Uzbekistan in improving the ecosystem for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to become catalysts for economic diversification and high value-added job creation, in line with the country's overall development strategy. The ecosystem will be improved through a simplified regulatory, policy, and institutional framework; diversified financial instruments; digital infrastructure; skilled labor; and improved financial and digital literacy.
The program is included in the country operations business plan for Uzbekistan, 2021-2023 of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and is aligned with ADB's country partnership strategy for Uzbekistan, 2019-2023. It is also aligned with ADB's Strategy 2030 operational priorities 1, 2, 3 and 6, which support SME development, quality job creation, gender equality, and strengthening institutional capacity and governance. Improving the ecosystem for SME development requires parallel multisector policy, institutional, and process reforms. In Uzbekistan, the situation is compounded by the multiplicity of agencies involved and the ongoing restructuring of some of these agencies, including the Small Business Entrepreneurship Development Agency (SBEDA) which requires substantial capacity building to lead reforms effectively. The coordination necessary to enable each subprogram to, individually and collectively, achieve meaningful improvements using well-sequenced, cross-sector reforms across many weak agencies, is the key rationale for a two-subprogram policy-based programmatic approach. The approach will also help the SBEDA to become an effective host institution for future SME development interventions through a sector development program or a results-based program.

title.narrative: Project/Program Completion Report
Policy 1 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Jan 01, 2021 - Nov 30, 2021

description.narrative:
Action 1: To ensure effective and efficient governance of the public credit guarantee (PCG) scheme for SMEs: (i) Ministry of Economic Development and Poverty Reduction (MOEDPR), in accordance with Order No. 35 aligned the State Fund for Support of Entrepreneurial Activity (State Fund) with the World Bank's 16 principles for Partial Credit Guarantees (PCG) by; a) operationalizing separate and more transparent accounting systems for the guarantee and interest compensation windows, b) operationalizing a transparent operational framework for the issuance and management of guarantees with clear eligibility and qualification criteria, and introducing climate change risk management considerations into the environment and social management system (ESMS) used for project screening, c) operationalizing an effective risk management framework with a risk-based pricing policy and transparent claims management process, and d) operationalizing a Management Information System with quarterly reporting, external audit and variance analysis against budgets; and (ii) Presidential Decree No. 6263 established an independent board of directors for the PCG which is now functioning. Target date: 2021-11-30
Action 2: To ensure that the State Fund expands PCGs to women's business, (i) Ministry of Finance (MOF) approved the allocation of SUM200 billion to the State Fund in the 2021 state budget, and further funds will be allocated on an annual basis on the demand of the State Fund to achieve issuance of at least 25% of new guarantees to women's businesses, and (ii) government approved a microenterprise- focused PCG product (with a higher guarantee ratio of 70%-75% and a low maximum loan amount cap of $20,000). Target date: 2021-11-30
Action 3: To expand access to finance by enabling the use moveable collateral, including accounts receivables and warehousing receipt financing, as security in financial contracts: (i) CBU abolished CBU Regulation 953 "On Procedures for conducting factoring operations by commercial banks on the territory of Uzbekistan," and (ii) CBU abolished in August 2021, the requirements (approved in 2000 under CBU Regulation No. 905) that constrained the effective used of moveable collateral in SME credit financing by commercial banks. Target date: 2021-11-30
Action 4: To: (i) promote financial innovations (FinTech, crowdfunding, etc.) to support SME financing, (ii) promote non-collateral-based lending to SMEs by expanding credit-history information, and (iii) support development of the nonbank finance sector's ability to serve SMEs, CBU submitted for COM approval the law on NonBank Credit Institutions and Microfinance Activities comprising: (i) legislative amendments allowing the creation of a regulatory sandbox, (ii) obligating leasing, and selected retail companies to provide credit-history information to the credit bureau, and (iii) defining the scope of services and governance principles of factoring organizations, microfinance institutions, and pawnshops and the corresponding regulatory role of the Central Bank of Uzbekistan (CBU). Target date: 2021-11-30
Action 1: To ensure effective regulation of PCGs and other innovative financial instruments (i) Government will adopt amendments to Central Bank (CBU) mandate; and (ii) CBU will adopt revised regulation on prudent capital relief measures on guaranteed loans. Target date: 2023-12-31
